questions.question: Predict the shape, hybridisation and bond angle of the following molecules using VSEPR theory: (a) PCl₅ (b) SF₆ (c) BeCl₂ (d) H₂S.
questions.solution:
**(a) PCl₅** — P has 5 valence electrons, all used in bonding; no lone pair. Steric number = 5 → **sp³d**, shape **trigonal bipyramidal**. Three equatorial bonds at $120^\circ$, axial–equatorial at $90^\circ$, axial–axial at $180^\circ$.

**(b) SF₆** — S has 6 valence electrons, all used in bonding; no lone pair. Steric number = 6 → **sp³d²**, shape **octahedral**. All adjacent bonds at $90^\circ$ and opposite pairs at $180^\circ$.

**(c) BeCl₂** — Be has only 2 valence electrons and forms 2 bonds with no lone pair. Steric number = 2 → **sp**, shape **linear**, angle $180^\circ$.

**(d) H₂S** — S has 6 valence electrons; 2 are used in bonding and 2 lone pairs remain. Steric number = 4 → approximately **sp³**, shape **bent (angular/V-shaped)**. The two lone pairs squeeze the bonds together so the angle is slightly less than the tetrahedral value, about **$92^\circ$** (compare $104.5^\circ$ in water, where O is more electronegative and the lone pairs are held closer to the nucleus).
questions.knowledgeNote: Five and six electron domains give trigonal bipyramidal (sp³d) and octahedral (sp³d²) shapes respectively.
